meta.subtitle: AI work and margins are improving, but growth has slowed and the largest clients carry a growing share of revenue

analystCommentary:
Grid Dynamics is in the middle of a shift that the second quarter of 2026 shows clearly. AI work is growing and gross margin is improving, while overall revenue growth has slowed to single digits and GAAP profit is close to zero.

At $8.09 on October 2, 2026 the shares sit between the 52-week low of $5.11 and the high of $10.21. The Street is mostly positive, with 5 Buy and 1 Hold ratings and a consensus target of $9.20, implying +13.8%.

The balance sheet offers some support (see Financials). What limits the upside is concentration in a few top customers (see Risks).

We rate GDYN HOLD with an $8–$10 target range.

executiveSummary.companyOverview:
Grid Dynamics Holdings, Inc. provides enterprise artificial intelligence and digital transformation services in North America, Europe and internationally. Its work spans AI strategy and deployment, data modernization, cloud platform and product engineering, digital commerce platforms, and IoT and edge computing.

The company describes itself as an enterprise AI transformation partner for the Fortune 1000. Its GAIN engagement model is a development framework for software delivery in the AI era, built on collaboration between AI tools and engineers. It serves retail, technology, media and telecom, finance, consumer packaged goods and manufacturing, healthcare and pharma, and other verticals.

Grid Dynamics was founded in 2006, reports a single segment, and is headquartered in San Ramon, California, with delivery teams across the Americas, Europe and India.

thesis.body: The improving mix toward AI work and the margin program are real. Against that, revenue growth has slowed, GAAP earnings are thin, and growth leans on a few large technology clients. Our probability-weighted fair value is only modestly above the current price (see Valuation), which is not enough for a BUY.

catalysts: Third-quarter 2026 results against the company's revenue and Non-GAAP EBITDA guidance.
Progress on the 300 basis point margin commitment the CEO reaffirmed.
Continued growth in AI revenue as a share of the total.
Integration of Ekumen, which the CEO said strengthens the company's Physical AI capabilities.
risks: Rising dependence on a few top customers.
Disruption to delivery from the war in Ukraine and wider regional instability.
AI tools reducing demand for traditional outsourced engineering hours.
Profitability that rests on adjusted rather than GAAP measures.

financials.incomeCommentary:
FY25 revenue was $411.8M, up {+17.5%+}, after growth of 12.0% in FY24 and 0.8% in FY23. Growth has since slowed: second-quarter 2026 revenue was $108.2 million, up 7.0%, and first-half revenue rose 5.3%.

Gross margin is improving. It reached 36.6% in the second quarter against 34.1% a year earlier, after drifting down from 41.5% in FY21 to 34.6% in FY25. Income from operations turned positive, a 1.2% margin, but general and administrative expense rose 19.4%.

The counter-case is in the bottom line. Net income fell to $2.9 million, or $0.03 per diluted share, from $5.3 million, because other income fell 57.1%. Non-GAAP EBITDA rose to $14.7 million and Non-GAAP diluted EPS to $0.11, so the adjusted view is much stronger than the GAAP one.
financials.balanceCommentary:
Cash and cash equivalents were $298.4 million at June 30, 2026, down from $342.1 million at December 31, 2025. The excerpt we hold does not break out the uses of that cash. Our data reports no debt for FY21 to FY25; that is a gap in the data rather than a confirmed zero. The trailing current ratio is 7.22.

The cash balance supports the shares but is not a hard floor: it is less than half the market value and fell in the six months to June 30, 2026. It gives the company room for buybacks and acquisitions, and it cushions a holder if growth disappoints.
financials.cashflowCommentary:
Free cash flow was $25.3M in FY25, a 6.1% FCF margin, with capital expenditure of -$15.3M. The FCF margin has stayed in single digits in four of the last five years, peaking at 10.6% in FY23.

Cash generation weakened in 2026: cash provided by operating activities was $14.5 million for the six months ended June 30, 2026, against $23.7 million a year earlier. The trailing FCF yield is 2.4%, which gives a holder little cash return at the current price. Better margins need to show up in cash flow, not only in Non-GAAP EBITDA.

valuation.multiplesCommentary:
At $8.09 GDYN trades at 1.6x trailing sales and 15.1x trailing EV/EBITDA. The 269.5x trailing P/E is not a useful measure given GAAP earnings (see Financials). On consensus, the NTM P/E is 17.4x and the forward P/E on FY27E is ~15.4x.

Those forward multiples rest on consensus EPS of $0.47 for FY26E and $0.53 for FY27E. Those figures are far above GAAP results and closer to the company's Non-GAAP earnings, so we read them as adjusted; the consensus basis is not stated.

Consensus FY26E revenue of $438.1M sits near the low end of the company's full-year guidance of $435.0 to $465.0 million. The Street is positive but not aggressive: a consensus target of $9.20, a median of $9.00 and a range of $7.00–$12.00.

We have no peer multiples to compare against, so we judge the price against the growth rate, the margin path and the cash balance.

scenarios.name: Bull
scenarios.driver: AI revenue keeps growing quickly, the margin commitment is delivered, and full-year revenue lands toward the top of guidance. The market pays a higher multiple for a faster-growing, more profitable business, taking the shares toward the upper end of the Street target range.

scenarios.name: Base
scenarios.driver: Revenue tracks consensus near the low end of guidance, margins improve gradually, and the multiple holds. The shares settle near the Street median target.

scenarios.name: Bear
scenarios.driver: A top technology client cuts spending, growth stalls, and the margin commitment slips. The shares fall back toward the lower part of the 52-week range.

valuation.scenarioCommentary:
Base carries the most weight because consensus and guidance already point to it. Bear gets more weight than Bull because the evidence for it is in the filing: the client concentration set out in Risks, and slower growth. Bull needs both faster growth and margin delivery at once.

The result is a weighted fair value of $8.80, an expected upside of +8.8% and a bear-case downside of -22.7%. That falls short of our BUY threshold.

Our $8–$10 target range brackets Base.

segments.name: Consolidated
segments.body: Grid Dynamics reports a single segment; the press release gives a vertical breakdown of second-quarter 2026 revenue. Technology, Media and Telecom was 31.8%, with TMT revenue up 36.4% year-over-year. Retail was 26.5%, Finance 22.9%, CPG and Manufacturing 10.9%, Healthcare and Pharma 1.9%, and Other 6.0%. The press release names TMT as the principal growth driver.

moatFactors.name: Engineering talent and delivery model
moatFactors.body: The company's skilled engineers across the Americas, Europe and India, and its GAIN delivery framework, are its main assets. The MD&A says it increasingly prioritizes experienced senior talent over volume staffing. Talent is not exclusive, though: the MD&A describes competition for IT professionals, and the 10-K describes intense competition for clients.

moatFactors.name: Client relationships
moatFactors.body: Long relationships with large enterprise clients drive most of the revenue, and several top accounts grew quickly in the quarter. The 10-K warns that the company has no long-term commitments from its clients, which may terminate contracts before completion or choose not to renew.

moatFactors.name: Partnerships
moatFactors.body: The MD&A describes co-development partnerships with major hyperscale cloud providers and leading platform AI companies, which support joint solutions and co-selling. Such partnerships help win work, but they are open to competitors as well.

businessMoat.durability: We rate the moat NONE. Grid Dynamics competes on talent and delivery quality in a services market where clients can switch providers and have no long-term commitments. Gross margin fell for most of the last five years before the recent recovery, which is consistent with limited pricing power. The company could build an advantage if its AI delivery model proves more productive than rivals' and lets it hold pricing, but the filing does not yet show that.

points: AI work is the growth engine. The press release puts AI revenue at 30.7% of the second-quarter total, and the CEO said it grew over 50% year-over-year for a second consecutive quarter.

Guidance implies a pickup: the company expects third-quarter revenue of $112.0 to $114.0 million and Non-GAAP EBITDA of $16.5 to $17.5 million. Meeting it would mean sequential growth from the second-quarter level.
The customer base is not widening: the company had 213 customers in the six months ended June 30, 2026, against 211 a year earlier.
Headcount fell to 4,838 from 5,013, while revenue rose. In our view, that fits the company's account of AI-driven productivity gains, but it also means growth no longer comes from adding engineers.

management.leadership: Per the proxy statement dated November 2025, which predates the 10-Q, the named executive officers were Leonard Livschitz, Chief Executive Officer and Director; Anil Doradla, Chief Financial Officer; and Yury Gryzlov, Chief Operating Officer and Chief Executive Officer of Grid Dynamics Europe. In the July 2026 earnings release, Mr. Livschitz said margin expansion is a top priority and that the company is on track to deliver its 300 basis point margin commitment. The release does not define which margin the commitment refers to, its base or its timing, so it is hard to hold management to precisely. The second-quarter gross margin gain is the evidence so far;
management.capitalAllocation:
Grid Dynamics pays no dividend. Share repurchases were small in FY25. The diluted weighted-average share count fell to 83.0 million in the second quarter of 2026 from 86.4 million a year earlier, and the company expects a basic share count of 81 - 82 million in the third quarter.

The CEO also cited the addition of Ekumen to strengthen the company's Physical AI capabilities; the release does not give the terms. The 10-K lists acquisitions as part of the strategy and warns that they can be difficult to integrate and can dilute stockholder value. With the cash balance described in Financials, the question for holders is the return earned on that cash, whether through buybacks or deals.
management.governance:
Per the proxy statement dated November 2025, the Board determined that Eric Benhamou, Lloyd Carney, Marina Levinson, Patrick Nicolet, Michael Southworth and Shuo Zhang are independent directors under SEC and Nasdaq rules. At the 2024 Annual Meeting, 98% of votes cast supported the Say-on-Pay proposal.

The proxy discloses that the CEO's spouse, son and step-son are employed by the company in non-executive roles; Mrs. Livschitz received total compensation in 2024 of approximately $236,988. The amounts are small relative to the company, but family employment is a related-party arrangement that the independent directors need to oversee. On balance, the independent majority and the strong Say-on-Pay vote point to adequate oversight. These facts predate the 10-Q and may have changed.
management.insiderOwnership:
Per the proxy, as of November 4, 2025 Beijing Teamsun Technology Co. Ltd. beneficially owned 16.4% of the common stock, based on a Schedule 13D/A filed in September 2024. Blackrock Inc. held 11.6%. Leonard Livschitz held 3.0%, and all executive officers and directors as a group held 6.5%.

In our view, a single holder of that size can carry weight in shareholder votes, and any sale of that stake could pressure the shares. Management's own stake gives it a meaningful but modest alignment with holders.

idiosyncratic: Customer concentration: the top customer was 17.4% of second-quarter revenue, against 15.1% a year earlier, and the top five were 43.5%, against 37.5%. The 10-K says revenue has historically been highly dependent on a limited number of clients and industries.

Geopolitical exposure: the MD&A says the military action in Ukraine continues and even worsens, that Russia could attempt to take control of company assets in Ukraine, and that the situations in Armenia and Serbia add uncertainty. Europe holds 3,011 of the company's 4,838 personnel.

AI substitution: the forward-looking statements list a decrease in demand for outsourced services as a result of AI or other technologies as a risk. In our view, the same tools that raise the company's productivity could reduce the billable work clients need.
Pricing and delivery: a majority of projects are time and materials, but an increasing number are fixed-price. The 10-K warns that misjudging the cost of service can make contracts unprofitable.
risks.systemic: The 10-K says revenue is highly dependent on clients primarily located in the U.S., so a U.S. economic downturn would hit demand. It also warns that macroeconomic conditions, inflationary pressures and market volatility could weigh on results, and the earnings release adds tariffs and the conflict with Iran to that list. In our view, discretionary technology spending is exposed to budget cuts in a slowdown.

body: HOLD, target range $8–$10, on the scenario math in Valuation.

We would move to BUY if third-quarter results land within guidance, the margin commitment shows up in GAAP profit and cash flow, and the share of revenue from the top clients stops rising. We would turn more cautious if a top client cuts spending or if the situation in Ukraine disrupts delivery.
